# BookNest

BookNest is a lightweight SaaS booking platform for service-based businesses that lets customers book and pay for appointments in under two minutes while giving owners real-time calendar control, automated reminders, and reliable no-show protection.

## Features

- Self-serve booking flow for salons, clinics, fitness studios, repair shops, and similar businesses
- Real-time calendar management with conflict prevention and configurable availability rules
- Stripe-backed deposit and prepayment support to reduce no-shows and protect revenue
- Automated SMS reminders and booking notifications for customers and staff
- Per-location subscription model designed for single-location businesses and multi-location franchises

## Tech stack

- Vanilla HTML
- Vanilla CSS
- Vanilla JavaScript
- FastAPI
- SQLite

## Demo login

The preview includes hardcoded demo credentials:

- Email: `demo@example.com`
- Password: `demo`

The demo experience runs against an in-browser fake backend powered by `localStorage`, so you can explore the product immediately without setting up any services. When deploying the real application, that preview backend is replaced by the FastAPI server in `backend/server.py`, which handles persistence and API behavior backed by SQLite.

## Quick start

1. Open `index.html` directly in your browser.
2. Or, if you want to inspect the API flow, run the backend and try requests with `curl`.
3. Log in with the demo credentials above and explore the booking flow.

Example API call:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/login -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"email":"demo@example.com","password":"demo"}'

## Architecture overview

BookNest is organized as a simple split between a frontend preview and a deployable backend.

- Frontend: a single-page experience built with vanilla HTML/CSS/JS
- Preview data layer: an in-browser fake backend using `localStorage` for fast local demoing
- Production data layer: FastAPI endpoints in `backend/server.py`
- Persistence: SQLite for lightweight, reliable storage
- Domain model: locations, staff, services, availability rules, bookings, and reminders

The frontend is designed to work immediately in preview mode, while the backend provides the real API surface for authenticated bookings, schedule integrity, and subscription-driven location management.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS entities (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    location_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    service_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    timezone TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UTC',
    is_active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (is_active IN (0, 1)),
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_entities_user_id ON entities(user_id);

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)


def get_token():
    response = client.post(
        "/api/auth/login",
        json={"email": "demo@booknest.com", "password": "demo123"},
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200
    data = response.json()
    assert "token" in data
    assert isinstance(data["token"], str)
    return data["token"]


def auth_headers():
    return {"Authorization": f"Bearer {get_token()}"}


def test_health_endpoint_returns_status():
    response = client.get("/api/health")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    data = response.json()
    assert "status" in data


def test_login_with_demo_credentials_returns_token():
    response = client.post(
        "/api/auth/login",
        json={"email": "demo@booknest.com", "password": "demo123"},
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200
    data = response.json()
    assert "token" in data
    assert data["token"]


def test_login_with_wrong_credentials_returns_401():
    response = client.post(
        "/api/auth/login",
        json={"email": "demo@booknest.com", "password": "wrong-password"},
    )
    assert response.status_code == 401


def test_get_entities_returns_list():
    response = client.get("/api/entities", headers=auth_headers())
    assert response.status_code == 200
    data = response.json()
    assert isinstance(data, list)


def test_create_entity_then_get_shows_new_item():
    payload = {"name": "Test Location", "type": "location"}
    create_response = client.post(
        "/api/entities",
        json=payload,
        headers=auth_headers(),
    )
    assert create_response.status_code == 200
    created = create_response.json()
    assert "id" in created

    list_response = client.get("/api/entities", headers=auth_headers())
    assert list_response.status_code == 200
    items = list_response.json()
    assert any(item.get("id") == created["id"] for item in items)


def test_delete_entity_removes_item():
    payload = {"name": "Delete Me", "type": "location"}
    create_response = client.post(
        "/api/entities",
        json=payload,
        headers=auth_headers(),
    )
    assert create_response.status_code == 200
    created = create_response.json()
    entity_id = created["id"]

    delete_response = client.delete(
        f"/api/entities/{entity_id}",
        headers=auth_headers(),
    )
    assert delete_response.status_code in (200, 204)

    list_response = client.get("/api/entities", headers=auth_headers())
    assert list_response.status_code == 200
    items = list_response.json()
    assert not any(item.get("id") == entity_id for item in items)
